verses.text: 57. This state of division into many nations is at once cosmic, social, and religious. It is intended to limit the pride of fallen humanity, (Cf. Acts 17:26–27.) united only in its perverse ambition to forge its own unity as at Babel. (Cf. Wis 10:5; Gen 11:4–6.) But, because of sin, both polytheism and the idolatry of the nation and of its rulers constantly threaten this provisional economy with the perversion of paganism. (Cf. Rom 1:18–25.)
